title: Microservices Examples
description: Small Microservices examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Small services with clear jobs
examples.description: A service is a part that does work for another part. Microservices divide an app by jobs, such as catalog search and lending.
examples.code:
Catalog service: book titles and authors
Loan service: who borrowed each copy
Browser: shows results to a learner

examples.title: Own the data you change
examples.description: A service should clearly own the data it changes. Other services use its interface rather than editing its tables directly.
examples.code:
Catalog owns Book records
Loans owns Loan records
Loans asks Catalog whether book 17 exists

examples.title: Contracts explain requests
examples.description: A contract describes the request fields and response fields. Both sides need to agree on their meaning.

examples.title: Direct calls can wait
examples.description: In a direct call, the caller waits for a reply. This is simple to follow but the caller depends on the other service responding.
examples.code:
Loans -> Catalog: is book 17 known?
Catalog -> Loans: yes
Loans continues

examples.title: Events announce something happened
examples.description: An event reports a past fact. Other services may react to it without the sender waiting for every reaction.
examples.code:
Event: BookBorrowed
Fields: eventId=81, copyId=203
Report service updates a daily count

examples.title: Duplicate messages are possible
examples.description: Message delivery can repeat. A consumer should recognise an event it has already handled.
examples.code:
Receive event 81: increase count; remember 81
Receive event 81 again: ignore duplicate
Count increases once

examples.title: Timeouts bound waiting
examples.description: A timeout sets a limit on waiting. The caller must choose a useful response when that limit passes.
examples.code:
Request begins at 0 ms
Timeout limit: 800 ms
No reply at 800 ms -> show a retry message

examples.title: Circuit breakers pause failing calls
examples.description: A circuit breaker stops repeated calls to a service that is failing. Later it allows a small trial to see whether recovery happened.
examples.code:
Several Catalog calls fail
Breaker opens: new calls fail fast
After a pause: allow one trial call

examples.title: Work across services needs recovery
examples.description: A multi-step business action can partly succeed. A recovery action, often called compensation, tries to undo an earlier step.
examples.code:
1. Reserve a book copy
2. Record the loan
If step 2 fails: release the reservation

examples.title: Versions protect callers
examples.description: A new contract version gives callers time to move. A safe added optional field is often easier than removing a field callers still need.

examples.title: Trace a request across parts
examples.description: A trace follows one request through several services. A shared trace ID connects the records.
examples.code:
trace-7 Browser -> Catalog
trace-7 Catalog -> Search index
trace-7 Search index took 900 ms

examples.title: Choose services only when needed
examples.description: Microservices bring independent releases and scaling, but add network calls and more operations work. Compare those costs before splitting an app.
examples.code:
Small team, one release schedule -> one well-organised app
Many teams, different scaling needs -> consider service boundaries
